touches.text: cairn:/// is the repo (from the environment, or from where bin/cairn itself lives); cairncommons:/// is the commons repo beside it; instance:/// is ~/.cairn; claude:/// is ~/.claude (the project's own .claude/ is already cairn:///.claude/, so it gets no second name); db:///cairn/table/row is the database; file:/// keeps its usual meaning, a real path on the filesystem, for what no root holds. claude: is also the Claude app's link scheme on this box: the resolver never hands an address to the system, so only a click on one opens the app.

A Dataref reads; it never writes. A write goes through the owner's gate (Law 6), and a db: address is read through db_domain's own client, never a second dial to 5432. An address on another box is read over the bus. WHY: one address system must not become one back door.
One that does not resolve is loud and names its address, never a value. A sieve reds a class-space config holding a plain value where a secret belongs.

question: the open-question door: a decision only the operator can make, bound to its ticket, answered in the operator's words. WHY: a spec choice is settled by Akien's head, recorded verbatim, never by a paragraph of CC's. USERS: tickets and CodeMother open them; the operator answers (7.4.2).

artifact: the one door a record of truth changes through, and the journal of who came through it (hash-chained, caller read from the kernel). WHY: errors are permanent in records of truth (Law 7), and the journal is what shows a record moved by hand. USERS: everyone who writes a record.

A retirement checks its callers in the same act as the deletion: nothing imports the module being deleted, and nothing runs the command or path being deleted. A file that only names it (a fixture, a record, a charter) is not a caller. Nothing checks afterwards. Why? Naming is history; only a caller breaks, and a caller that comes later breaks loudly on its own. A standing proof that a thing stays gone is history kept as code.
Evidence, a measurement, says what is. It settles what it measures, for everyone. Why? Because evidence ALWAYS wins.

dataref: one address for any stored record, in any format, and the thin class that reads it. WHY: a config, a ticket or a node can say WHERE a value lives without carrying it, so the repo stays shareable and a private value stays in ~/.cairn; and one way of pointing works across every format and every box. USERS: anything that reads stored data.

Dataref is the base class. Secret is its subclass: its str, repr and format are all **********, so a log line or an f-string cannot show it; .secret fetches the value at that moment. WHY: printing it by mistake shows stars, and every place a secret is unmasked is a .secret anyone can grep for. Prior art: pydantic's SecretStr, and fsspec for one interface over many stores (cited, not grafted).
corrosion: catches a constraint that stopped constraining with no decision behind it. WHY: drift with a decision behind it is the system learning; drift with none is decay.
